perspective:
From Arthur’s available perspective:

- I am Arthur Chung and I work with Teresa Ortega on community service projects.
- I noticed Teresa had been working hard and seemed overwhelmed. I asked if I could help.
- I heard Teresa say it was kind but she could manage, and that there was a lot to do.
- I told her self-care was important and offered to help so we could finish faster together. She accepted and asked for help organizing medical supplies. I agreed.
- I believed Teresa was hesitant because she wanted to prove her capability. I felt empathetic and wanted to reassure her that accepting help did not undermine her abilities.
- I told her I admired her self-reliance, but accepting help doesn’t mean she isn’t capable.
- I heard Teresa say she appreciated it, but wanted to show she could do it by herself.
- I told her teamwork can be more effective and it’s not about proving anything; it’s about getting the job done well. She agreed she sometimes needs to remind herself of that. I said we’re in this together and I support her.
- I believed she was still struggling. I felt frustrated that my help wasn’t yielding results and wanted another way to support her without making her feel inadequate.
- I told her I could see things were still tough and she shouldn’t feel she wasn’t doing a great job. I heard her say it had been a busy day and she felt behind.
- I suggested working together on tasks instead of me just helping her. She agreed. I said we’d tackle it as a team.
- I believed working together would ease her burden and improve efficiency. I felt hopeful and intended to fully commit to the collaborative approach.
- I told her I was hopeful the collaborative approach would make things easier. She said it already felt less overwhelming.
- I proposed handling the inventory while she managed patient records, checking in regularly. She agreed. I said we’d make it a productive day.
- I believed our collaboration strengthened our professional relationship and felt satisfied with the outcome.
- I told her our teamwork had paid off and we accomplished more together. She agreed it had been a great experience.
- I suggested continuing the collaborative approach in future projects. She said it was a fantastic idea and that we’d proven we can be efficient and effective as a team.
- I agreed and said I looked forward to our next project. She thanked me for being a supportive colleague.
